4. Complexity, allocation, and performance
5. Common gotchas and compiler-guided debugging
Do not reach for clone() as the first borrow-checker fix. Decide whether the algorithm needs ownership, a shared borrow, a mutable borrow, or a structural redesign using indices.
Iterator chains are lazy and commonly optimize well, but repeated collect(), clone(), String allocation, or HashMap construction can dominate small inputs.
Line-by-line reasoning checklist
Rc cycles leak because reference counts never reach zero; use Weak for non-owning back-links.

Recursive functions usually borrow the structure (&Node / &mut Node) while owning only small state. Returning references requires explicit lifetime relationships only when elision cannot express them.
RefCell borrow rules are checked at runtime; overlapping borrow_mut calls panic.
Rust lens 2: make ownership, borrowing, mutation, representation, and drop behavior explicit before optimizing.
Rust lens 6: make ownership, borrowing, mutation, representation, and drop behavior explicit before optimizing.
Shorten borrow scopes: read what you need, let the borrow end, then mutate. Entry APIs, split_at_mut, slice pattern matching, Option::take, mem::replace, and local temporaries are common tools.
String/&str indexing is byte-based at slicing boundaries; Unicode code points and grapheme clusters are different concepts.

The algorithmic idea is language-independent, but the implementation must make ownership, aliasing, mutation, failure, and allocation explicit. Prefer borrowing slices and references for read-only work, narrowly scoped &mut borrows for mutation, owned values when ownership transfer is the cleanest API, and smart pointers/interior mutability only when the data model genuinely requires shared topology.
Vec/slice traversal is usually cache-friendly. Rc/RefCell node graphs add pointer chasing, refcount updates, runtime borrow checks, and fragmented allocation.
What allocation happens?
What does the type system rule out before runtime?
Where does a mutable borrow begin and end?
Which line moves ownership?
Which lines only borrow?
Which operation can panic?
sort_by comparator must define a coherent ordering; prefer cmp/then_with instead of arithmetic subtraction.
usize underflow/overflow and index math deserve explicit boundary reasoning.
